ADMINISTRATION & MANAGEMENT Goals & Objectives, FY2027 | 3

Administration & Management The overall Administration & Management goal is to provide leadership within the WIC Nutrition Program to maximize the quality and effectiveness of WIC service delivery across Massachusetts. The primary objectives for FY27 are:

I. To improve program infrastructure, management, and participant access to services to continue progress toward greater coverage rates and maximized funding.

A. Continue to maintain and enhance Eos to incorporate necessary modifications, including new requirements, enhancements, and other state IT projects to improve service access, nutrition education, operations, health- related programming and evaluation, and data for nutrition and health surveillance.

B. Continue to support WIC EBT to maximize WIC participation at the retail vendor level and increase agency knowledge about participant food purchasing patterns. Support ongoing implementation and evaluation of the WIC online ordering project in partnership with Washington state and the Center for Nutrition and Health Impact.

C. Continue to monitor and enhance local program nutrition services and program performance, emphasizing quality as integral to program operations and excellent participant services.

1. Monitor the performance management system to engage in effective quality improvement at local programs, emphasizing health and operations outcome measures. Provide ongoing technical assistance to support optimal quality improvement efforts at state and local program levels.

2. Review and assess local program staffing, workflow, and participant service delivery to support participation demands, ensure effective, efficient program operations, and improve outcomes.

3. Monitor and evaluate local WIC programs, providing technical assistance and taking follow up action, as needed.

D. Continue to support and strengthen participant-centered nutrition service delivery through the provision of ongoing training and technical assistance to local program staff.

E. Support the implementation of a statewide breastfeeding strategic plan, ensuring WIC’s role as a key partner in improving the Commonwealth’s breastfeeding outcomes.

F. Utilize WIC service and outcome data to monitor trends in the Program; design and implement strategies to improve performance and impact.

G. Assist in attaining statewide assigned service level of 125,351 participants.

1. Utilize the Caseload & Funding Allocation Methodologies—including the annual WIC Needs Assessment and standards for clinic location, staffing and other program operations—to allocate caseload and related support funding to local programs and continue to reflect community needs.

2. Support WIC local agencies to operate in newly defined service areas for the contract cycle beginning 7/1/2026.

3. Continue social marketing activities, including the use of Facebook, Geofencing, Twitter, Instagram and content marketing, and launch new activities to promote earlier prenatal enrollment to maximize program participation as part of the ongoing statewide multicultural public awareness campaign in support of local program outreach and continued expansion of access to WIC.

4. Facilitate coordination of WIC participant services—emphasizing cross referrals and outreach activities at the state and local levels and utilizing local program community coordinators—with other program services in the Nutrition Division, other programs in the DPH Bureaus of Family Health & Nutrition, Community Health and Prevention, Immunization, and Lead Poisoning Prevention as well as the Departments of Transitional Assistance, Early Education and Care, Agricultural Resources, Children and Families, the Division of Unemployment Assistance, MassHealth, and the Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities. Ensure close collaboration with community nutrition programs serving the maternal and child health populations such as Head Start, Early Intervention and the Maternal and Child Health home visiting programs.

5. Coordinate data sharing to improve outreach and referrals between WIC and other Bureau of Family Health & Nutrition programs, other DPH maternal and child health programs, and with the MassHealth/Medicaid and SNAP programs.

6. Continue to strengthen WIC relationships with clinicians and managed care plans, the MassHealth/Medicaid Program, and statewide childcare, welfare, and immigrant organizations to provide opportunities for increased referrals to WIC and coordinated, comprehensive health care for participants.

H. Continue analysis, policy development, cost containment and monitoring of the implementation of and any updates to the federal Food Package Rule.

1. Continue to collaborate with other states in the New England & Tribal Organization (NEATO) to monitor the infant formula rebate contract and implement the contract that begins on October 1, 2026.

2. Continue implementation of the 2024 Food Package Rule, monitoring participant purchasing patterns and preparing for additional updates, such as the vitamin D requirement for yogurt.

I. Continue to focus on customer service at local WIC programs and authorized WIC retailers to address participant recruitment and retention issues and enhance access to services.

FISCAL Goals & Objectives, FY2027 | 7

Fiscal The overall Fiscal goal is to maximize utilization of available funds and ensure timely and accurate receipt, disbursement and accounting of all funds used to support program services throughout Massachusetts. The primary objectives for FY27 are:

I. To monitor and project food costs and participation in conjunction with other program units to provide optimal nutritional benefits at a reasonable cost.

A. In consideration of economic fluctuations, track monthly food expenditures, funds, infant formula rebates, and participation and adjust components to ensure maximum participation within funding parameters. Make projections using available data tracking systems.

1. Maintain enhanced automated food cost and participation projection programs.

2. Collaborate with other program units to develop WIC participation projections.

3. Develop and present projections reflecting actual and potential changes in food costs, inflation, participation, and funding by looking at detailed food redemption data and daily caseload changes – inclusive of number of online applications and results of texting campaigns.

B. Prepare reports that summarize the fiscal year food cost experience in aggregate and by food type, review historical trends, forecast food costs, and highlight monitoring issues for the future.

C. Continue to balance food costs with participant food choices.

1. Collaborate with other program units on formula and food package development issues and any required changes.

2. Collaborate with Nutrition Services, Operations and Systems to follow food item activities and cost containment strategies in other states, implementing and integrating appropriate changes, as needed.

3. Participate in the development and evaluation of the annual Participant Satisfaction Survey

II. To manage federal grants and ensure proper, timely disbursement of funds for services.

A. Continue to monitor transfer and reconciliation of the draw down of federal funds.

B. Continue to complete timely and accurate ASAP justifications for weekly expenditures report in conjunction with the DPH Accounting office and the Comptroller.

NUTRITION SERVICES Goals & Objectives, FY2027 | 12

Nutrition Services The overall Nutrition Services goal is to improve the nutritional health of women, infants and children through the delivery of culturally appropriate, effective, high-quality nutrition services. The primary objectives for FY27 are:

I. To oversee the delivery of nutrition services that are responsive to WIC participants.

A. Provide consultation and technical assistance to the local program management team, senior nutritionist, program director, and nutrition staff in the planning, provision, and evaluation of nutrition services. Provide technical assistance in partnership with formal training opportunities for new senior nutritionists.

B. Coordinate activities of the Nutritionists’ Work Group to solicit input and feedback from and exchange information with local program staff for the planning, provision, and evaluation of WIC nutrition services.

C. Provide local programs with technical assistance to expand and strengthen participant-centered nutrition assessment, counseling, and education as well as provide culturally and linguistically appropriate nutrition services utilizing emotion-based techniques to enhance positive behavior outcomes.

D. Ensure that resources on motivational interviewing and technical assistance are available regularly to local programs and provide training as needed.

E. Collaborate with The Learning Center (TLC) to provide new staff training to nutritionists, senior nutritionists and CPAs; continuing education opportunities including online training modules; orientation to programmatic and service delivery changes; and technical assistance related to specific nutrition service components identified as part of the Local Program Evaluation (LPE) process.

F. Develop educational activities, training materials, and collaborative tools to promote healthy weight through nutrition education and physical activity initiatives for WIC participants.

G. Coordinate activities of the Nutrition Education Task Force to solicit local program input and develop creative ideas, strategies, and tools that are culturally and linguistically appropriate and participant- centered to facilitate active and meaningful learning by WIC participants. Review and revise existing nutrition education materials to be digitally accessible and reflect local program needs and emotion-based participant-centered services. Continue to expand access to nutrition and breastfeeding educational materials for participants and staff online and via the WICShopper app.
